 Common Judgment

The petitioners of MVC No.4666/23 c/w. 4667/23 &
4668/2023 have filed these petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by them in the road traffic accident occurred on 03.06.2023.
2. The petitioner of MVC No.4666/2023 has filed application to club MVC Nos. 4667/23 & 4668/2023 with it.
The said application came to be allowed on the ground that the respondents in all the cases is one and the same and the injuries were caused from the same accident.
Hence, all these cases are clubbed together to lead common evidence.

3. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follow:-
 On 03.06.2023 at about 5.30 p.m. when they were proceeding in an Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-05-AD-9360 as inmates,
near Sai Baba Temple Junction, Vishweshwaraiah Road, Hulimavu Arakere Road, Hulimavu, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the  SCCH-08 4 MVC No.4666/23 c/w. 4667/23 & 4668/2023 Car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MG-5501 came in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the Auto of the petitioners, caused the accident and as a result, they sustained grievous injuries.

It is contended that, immediately they were taken to nearby Nano hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein petitioner in MVC No.4666/23 was taken first aid, thereafter for higher treatment she was shifted to Fortis hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and petitioners in MVC No.4667/23 and 4668/2023 were taken treatment as an inpatient at Nano Hospital, Bengaluru.
It is contended that they have spent huge amount for treatment and medical expenses.

4. It is further stated that prior to the accident, petitioners in MVC No.4666/213, 4667/2023 & 4668/23 were hale and healthy and were working as Software Engineer, Manager and Tailor respectively and the petitioner in MVC No.4666/23 was earning Rs.61,000/- per month and petitioner in MVC No.4667/23 was earning Rs.75,000/- p.m. and petitioner in MVC No.4668/23 was earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.

This respondent has denied the issuance of policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of the offending Car bearing Reg No. KA-51-MG-5501 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

It is the case of the petitioners in both the claim petitions that, on 03.06.2023 at about 5.30 p.m. when they were proceeding  SCCH-08 7 MVC No.4666/23 c/w. 4667/23 & 4668/2023 in an Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-05-AD-9360 as inmates,

sentences.text:
According to the version of petitioners of the MVC 4666/23 and 4667/23, the accident happened near Sai Baba Temple junction, Vishweshwaraiah Road, Hulimavu Arakere road,
Hulimavu, Bengaluru in the Auto bearing Reg. No. KA-05-AD-9360 as passengers at that time, the driver of the Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-MG-5501 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the Auto in which the petitioners were traveling as passengers and caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 and P4 being the Spot Mahazar and also Sketch which was prepared at the time of Spot Mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 and 4 it reflects that the injured were traveling in the Auto as a passengers and accident occurred at Junction, the driver of the Car came in a negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the Auto as per Ex.P3 and 4 which is mahazer and Sketch.

As per these documents accident the width of the road is 40 feet,
 SCCH-08 8 MVC No.4666/23 c/w. 4667/23 & 4668/2023 the driver of the car came from Arakere road and dashed to the right side of the Auto and the said place is junction, car came from Arakere road towards Vishweshwaraiah road to take right diversion.
If the driver of the car drove it in a normal speed by observing on going vehicles in the junction, then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Added more, the contents of Ex.P7 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle and also lift side of both vehicle damaged.
Further more, even the chargesheet as per Ex.P8 was also filed as against the driver of the bus.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P3 and 4 coupled with Ex.P8 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the Car driver.
In the arguments counsel of Respondent raised the point that the driver of the auto has also contributed in the accident, respondent has not examined the eye witness of the accident.

The PW1 and 2 who are inmates of the auto are one of the eye witnesses to the incident and in the cross examination of these witnesses, respondent has not elicited any evidence from their mouth regarding the negligent driving by the auto driver.
13. The driver of the car has not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part.

After the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of the Car bearing registration No.KA-51-MG-5501 concluding that the accident was occurred only due to his negligence.
There is no reason to take a different view.

Therefore, I hold that the accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the  SCCH-08 9 MVC No.4666/23 c/w. 4667/23 & 4668/2023 Sandhya Guha Thakurta vs Vutukuri Nageshwarrao on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196166217/

ISSUE No.2 in MVC 4666/2023:
14. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove the disability.
Hence, she is not entitled for compensation for loss of future income on account of permanent disability.

15. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
 Petitioner has produced wound certificate at Ex.P9 and 10 which reveals that the petitioner has sustained Facial degloving injury with right eyebrow crush injury.

The doctor has opined that,
the said injury is grievous in nature.

Further the Ex.P13 Discharge Summary of Fortis Hospital reveals that petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital from 04.06.2023 to 06.06.2023 for a period of 3 days and she also admitted in Nano Hospital on 03.06.2023 and discharged on 04.06.2023.
Considering these aspects, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.20,000/- towards pain and sufferings.
16. MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The petitioner has produced Medical bill worth Rs.4,16,306/-
as per Ex.P14.
I have examined the same.

Since the petitioner was treated as inpatient and undergone treatment, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioner to the tune of Rs.4,16,306/- and she is entitled for the same.

Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.10,000/-
under this head.

sentences.text: Liability:
Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA- 51-MG-5501.
The respondent No.2 has not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, 1 st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2 nd respondent being the insurer shall indemnify the 1 st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative in MVC No.4666/2023 and MVC No.4667/2023 and issue No.2 in MVC No.4668/2023 is in the Negative.
31. Issue No.3 in all the claim petitions

: In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2 as above, I pass the following:

. 4666/2023 and MVC No.4667/2023 are allowed in part with cost and MVC No.4668/2023 is dismissed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,62,306/-(Rupees Four lakhs sixty two thousand three hundred and six only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the compensation amount, entire amount shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and due verification.

MVC.No. 4667/2023:
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.92,780/-(Rupees Ninety two thousand seven hundred and eighty only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
